Stated Claim / Post Context:
Hastings man gets two years in jail for the baby found in ditch case

A man was sentenced in the case of a 15-month-old baby who was found in an Adams County ditch last year.

Actual Article Body:
HASTINGS, Neb. (KSNB) - A Hastings man will spend time in jail in the case of a 15-month-old baby who was found in an Adams County ditch last year.

Court records show Austin Hendrick, 31, was sentenced to one year in jail for misdemeanor child abuse, and an additional year in jail for obstruction of a police officer. A related charge of felony child abuse was dropped in a plea bargain.

Hendrick will receive 280 days for time served on each count. He is also ordered to pay court fees following his release.

On Oct. 4, 2025, a 15-month-old child was found alive in a ditch in rural Adams County by a concerned citizen.

The sheriff’s office said deputies were sent to the 2,000 block of South Marian Road just after 8 a.m. that morning, after a concerned citizen reported finding the baby.

At the time the child was found healthy and unharmed.

Court records that would detail what led to Hendrick’s involvement are sealed.

However, during a court hearing Monday, it was revealed that the child was in Hendrick’s care at the time, but Hendrick’s attorney said his client said he was not the one who abandoned the baby in the ditch. It was also revealed that Hendrick failed to call law enforcement immediately after he discovered the child was missing.

During Monday’s hearing, Judge Morgan Farquhar said that demonstrated Hendrick’s negligence.

“It is a miracle that this turned out the way it did for this child, considering the facts and the circumstances,” Farquhar said. “It doesn’t take much of an imagination to think what could have happened. And I think you realize that, or at least I hope you do. I hope you realize how serious this case is.”

Hendrick did speak during the sentencing where he said he was sorry.

“I love her. I love her family. I consider them family and will forever regret the actions that made this horrible event happen,” Hendrick said.

Local4 has reached out to the Adams County Attorney to find out if any other persons have been charged in connection with the case. We are waiting to hear back.
